Dangote replaces NSSF in KPC boardroom shake-up

Monday, November 16, 2026 - 6 min read

By  Kepha Muiruri

Business Reporter

Nation Media Group

Thank you for reading businessdailyafrica.com

Show plans
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 54:28
Instaread

Nigerian billionaire businessman Aliko Dangote is set to replace the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) on the board of Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC) after acquiring a 24.9 percent stake in the midstream oil company last month.

The change is part of a shake-up expected on the board of KPC, which will also see five Kenyan directors exit the company at the end of its upcoming annual general meeting (AGM) on December 2.

Mr Dangote, who acquired a significant stake in KPC through Greenview Oil Trading Corp from local institutional investors including the NSSF, is expected to nominate a director to the board ahead of the AGM.

The nominee will replace Ronald Nyamosi who is currently the NSSF’s general manager for finance and investments and has served as the alternate director to the fund’s CEO.

KPC’s articles of association require significant institutional shareholders in the company to nominate a single director to the board.

“So as long as oil marketing companies (OMCs) jointly, or any other shareholder, hold at least 20 percent of the issued capital of the company, 30 days before the date of each annual general meeting shall be entitled to nominate one director to the board,” say the KPC’s articles of association.

Greenview Oil, a Dangote affiliate company, replaced the NSSF as KPC’s second-largest investor through a block trade of the pipeline operator’s shares last month when it acquired a 24.99 percent stake in the business.

Greenview Oil is a foreign registered entity, and its ownership records do not sit with the Business Registration Service (BRS) as per queries run by this publication with the local business registry.

The NSSF sold partial stakes in KPC alongside other State-linked pension schemes including the Public Service Superannuation Fund (PSSF) and the County Pension Fund (CPF).

Smaller schemes including Lapfund, Laptrust, Kenya Power Pension Scheme and the Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) Pension Scheme made full exits from KPC.

The Dangote oil firm is now KPC’s second-largest shareholder and is sandwiched between the Kenyan government’s residual 35 percent stake, following the sale of a 65 percent stake in the firm at an initial public offering (IPO) in March this year, and the Uganda government’s 20.15 stake, held through the Uganda National Oil Corporation (UNOC).

No other shareholder holds a significant stake, with the ownership of local pension schemes combined falling below 15 percent.

The ownership structure hands the Nigerian tycoon influence and voting rights on the strategic direction of the firm.

Mr Dangote has said he plans to invest $1.5bn (Sh195 billion) to expand KPC’s pipeline network in the middle of building a second 700,000-barrel-a-day refinery in Lamu worth Sh2.1 trillion.

This represents an ambitious attempt to build an integrated African refining, storage and distribution business, with Kenya serving as a regional hub for eastern Africa and Namibia for southern Africa.

KPC’s 1,300km pipeline network transports diesel, petrol and jet fuel from the port of Mombasa across Kenya, supplying both the domestic market and neighbouring countries including Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, South Sudan and Rwanda.

Mr Dangote paid about Sh42.5 billion for the KPC stake, translating to a price of Sh9.36 per share, which was a premium to the prevailing market cost.

Read: Dangote buys 24pc stake of Kenya Pipeline Company

The governments of Kenya and Uganda have exercised their rights to nominate five directors to the board, all of whom already sit on the firm’s governing body.

Three of the five nominated directors have been seconded by Kenya’s Treasury: Faith Boinett who currently serves as the board chairperson, Samson Burgei (currently the alternate director to the Treasury Cabinet Secretary) and Meshack Kidenda.

Ms Boinett is expected to remain on the board of KPC despite pressure from a workers’ union that has filed a court petition.

The Kenya Petroleum Oil Workers Union alleged that Ms Boinett’s links to Fastnett Energy Limited, a company that does business with KPC, raises conflicts of interest.

Last month, the High Court struck out a petition challenging her appointment by President William Ruto as KPC chairperson, noting that it lacked jurisdiction to hear the dispute.

President Ruto appointed Ms Boinett on December 19, 2025 for a three-year term effective from December 23 of the same year.

Uganda has also used its powers to back the retention of its two current serving directors Ramathan Ggoobi (the Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Finance) and Irene Pauline Bateeba (Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Energy).

Five current directors, all of Kenyan nationality — Joyce Emanikor, Mutungwa Wambua, Christopher Karani, Martha Miano and Irene Wachira — are expected to retire from the board at the end of the December AGM after filling what KPC describes as casual vacancies.

Mr Dangote’s entry to KPC board is expected to come at a pivotal time as the company gears to appoint a substantive chief executive officer.

The billionaire businessman is expected to help influence the hiring of KPC’s next CEO even as the Kenyan and Ugandan governments control the process of appointing the firm’s leader.

KPC’s board failed to pick a new CEO earlier this year as cracks emerged as to whether the firm should initiate recruitment of a new managing director without a fully constituted board. The post fell vacant after Joe Sang resigned following a fuel scandal in April this year, which came a month after KPC’s IPO.

Pius Mwendwa has served as the acting CEO since Mr Sang’s departure.

He previously served as the firm’s general manager in charge of finance.

Mr Dangote is viewed as a strategic investor in KPC and is expected to oversee additional investments into the pipeline company, including linking the firm to his East African refinery, which is currently under construction in Lamu.

KPC is expected to play a pivotal role in setting up key distribution infrastructure, to and from the refinery, including a heated pipeline from Kenya’s oil fields in Turkana to the Lamu facility, and a network of regional distribution pipelines including a line linking the refinery with Ethiopia.

Mr Dangote’s entry into KPC’s ownership has helped drive KPC’s share price rally, which had been previously stuck around the Sh9 IPO price.

KPC’s stock reached an all-time price of Sh16.60 in the wake of Mr Dangote’s shares purchase but has since cooled off to close at Sh9.64 on Monday. The 52-week high price presented an 84.4 percent gain from the Sh9 listing price.

Create profiles for personalised advertising

Create profiles to personalise content

Information about your activity on this service (for instance, forms you submit, non-advertising content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (such as your previous activity on this service or other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (which might for example include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present content that appears more relevant based on your possible interests, such as by adapting the order in which content is shown to you, so that it is even easier for you to find content that matches your interests.

Use profiles to select personalised content

Content presented to you on this service can be based on your content personalisation profiles, which can reflect your activity on this or other services (for instance, the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects. This can for example be used to adapt the order in which content is shown to you, so that it is even easier for you to find (non-advertising) content that matches your interests.

View details

Measure advertising performance

Information regarding which advertising is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine how well an advert has worked for you or other users and whether the goals of the advertising were reached. For instance, whether you saw an ad, whether you clicked on it, whether it led you to buy a product or visit a website, etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of advertising campaigns.

View details

Measure content performance

Information regarding which content is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine whether the (non-advertising) content e.g. reached its intended audience and matched your interests. For instance, whether you read an article, watch a video, listen to a podcast or look at a product description, how long you spent on this service and the web pages you visit etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of (non-advertising) content that is shown to you.

View details

Understand audiences through statistics or combinations of data from different sources

Reports can be generated based on the combination of data sets (like user profiles, statistics, market research, analytics data) regarding your interactions and those of other users with advertising or (non-advertising) content to identify common characteristics (for instance, to determine which target audiences are more receptive to an ad campaign or to certain contents).

View details

Develop and improve services

Information about your activity on this service, such as your interaction with ads or content, can be very helpful to improve products and services and to build new products and services based on user interactions, the type of audience, etc. This specific purpose does not include the development or improvement of user profiles and identifiers.

View details

Use limited data to select content

Content presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type, or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times a video or an article is presented to you).

Special purposes

Ensure security, prevent and detect fraud, and fix errors

Your data can be used to monitor for and prevent unusual and possibly fraudulent activity (for example, regarding advertising, ad clicks by bots), and ensure systems and processes work properly and securely. It can also be used to correct any problems you, the publisher or the advertiser may encounter in the delivery of content and ads and in your interaction with them.

Deliver and present advertising and content

Certain information (like an IP address or device capabilities) is used to ensure the technical compatibility of the content or advertising, and to facilitate the transmission of the content or ad to your device.

View details

Save and communicate privacy choices

Features

Link different devices

In support of the purposes explained in this notice, your device might be considered as likely linked to other devices that belong to you or your household (for instance because you are logged in to the same service on both your phone and your computer, or because you may use the same Internet connection on both devices).

Identify devices based on information transmitted automatically

How this consent management platform (CMP) works:

CMP privacy choices

Storage, duration, and usage details

The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
  • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
  • For apps, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
  • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.
